extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and prospective applicants to NICHD K-series career development awards (postdocs, clinician-scientists, early-career faculty) seeking NICHD-specific policy guidance
extracted.subtask_description: NICHD-specific FAQs and policy guidance for applying to and administering NIH K-series career development awards (K01, K08, K23, K25, K99/R00, etc.), including eligibility, budget limits, documentation, transition procedures, and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01: NICHD-supported research areas and applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD accepts K01 applications for only three specific research areas: Medical Rehabilitation Research, Child Abuse and Neglect, and Population Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical Rehabilitation Research: Applicants must have clinical training in a rehabilitation-related profession (e.g., physical therapy, occupational therapy, registered nurse, speech and language pathologist), possess a doctoral level degree (Ph.D., D.Eng., D.Ed.), and be committed to an independent investigator career in medical rehabilitation. Child Abuse and Neglect: Applicants should have relevant discipline experience and propose a mentored research program using novel or interdisciplinary approaches. Population Research: Defined as demographic, behavioral, and social scientific research on fertility, family/household structures, mortality/morbidity, migration, immigration, population and the environment, and population distribution and characteristics. The K01 in Population Research is intended to provide mentored training for (a) demographers needing additional technical/scientific skills, (b) population researchers seeking cross-disciplinary experience, and (c) investigators from other disciplines proposing new training in demography/population research. The program is generally limited to assistant professor–level individuals who have not secured major research funding (see program announcement), though recent associate professors or established investigators making a major change may be eligible (prior R01 allowable). All K01 applicants must justify the need for mentored training and explain how it will facilitate cutting-edge research in the named fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: K02: NICHD participation
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD no longer participates in the K02 program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the referenced notice (NOT-HD-14-009) for details and seek alternative mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: K08: NICHD support and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD sponsors the K08 mechanism for research relevant to its mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: provide support and protected time for intensive supervised research career development in biomedical and behavioral research, including translational research. Eligibility is limited to those with a clinical doctoral degree. Clinically trained individuals conducting patient-oriented research should apply for the K23 instead. Consult the Program Announcement and the IC-specific 'Table of IC-specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts' for institute-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: K23: NICHD support, purpose, and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD sponsors the K23 Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award for investigators committed to patient-oriented research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals with a clinical degree who are interested in biomedical research that is not patient-oriented should apply for K08. K23 applicants must document how they will finance the research (see K23 budget limits) and should follow NICHD guidance on describing mentor commitments, institutional support, and resource contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: K23 budget limits and documentary expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The K23 allows a maximum of $25,000 for research support and $100,000 plus fringe benefits for salary per year; the remainder of project costs must come from other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must clearly explain needed resources and their sources or reviewers may deem the project not feasible. Mentors and collaborators should list active support in their biosketches and document willingness to participate in personal statements and in Item 8: Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s) (six-page limit). Institutional support letters and Item 10 (Facilities and Other Resources) may describe additional resources. Pull all information together in the Research Strategy so reviewers see how the project will be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: K24: NICHD participation
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD no longer participates in the K24 mid-career award in patient-oriented research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek alternate mechanisms or check NIH-wide announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: K25: NICHD participation
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD sponsors the K25 mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific institute requirements are listed in the Program Announcement's 'Table of IC-specific Information, Requirements, and Staff Contacts.' Applicants should consult that table for NICHD-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00: intended applicants and program purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD offers K99/R00 awards in areas relevant to its mission. The program is designed for postdoctoral fellows whose formal research training is nearly complete and who expect to find a tenure-track or equivalent faculty position within 2 years of receiving the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to consult NICHD Scientific/Research Contact to choose among career development mechanisms, determine eligibility, and assess project relevance. The award is two-phase (K99 then R00) within a single application spanning five years; awardees must spend at least 1 year on the K99 phase and the program presumes transition to R00 within the intended timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 eligibility window and timing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The K99/R00 program is intended for those 0 to 4 years post-degree for initial submissions and re-submissions, with most applicants applying in the third or early fourth postdoctoral year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess whether the applicant is likely to obtain a tenure-track or equivalent position within the 2-year K99 timeframe. Applicants should evaluate competitiveness (publications, technical experience) relative to peers. If 'too junior,' consider waiting or applying for an F32 individual postdoctoral fellowship first (which may strengthen a subsequent K99).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of research assistant professors/instructors for K99
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who already hold independent research faculty or tenure-track appointments, or who have received independent grant funding as PI, are not eligible for K99/R00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many non–tenure-track positions may still be considered non-independent and eligible. Eligibility for different faculty appointments is detailed in Section III.1 of the K99/R00 Program Announcement (PA-16-077).

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 budget and effort requirements (K99 phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 budgets should specify the candidate's current institutional base salary with a minimum 75% effort. NICHD maximum allowable amounts for the K99 phase are salary up to $75,000 plus fringe benefits and up to $25,000 for research support costs per year (direct cost amounts). Indirect costs are added at an 8% rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to request the full $25,000 for research expenses. Fringe benefits should be added to requested salary. Prepare detailed budgets for K99 years (years 1–2) as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 budget limits and preparation (R00 phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum total cost budget for the independent (R00) phase is $249,000 per year (includes direct and indirect costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the candidate may move institutions, salary, research expenses, and F&A for R00 are usually unknown; prepare hypothetical budgets for R00 years 3–5. R00 budgets will be requested again at transition submission by the R00 sponsoring institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and content of K99 and R00 research plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The K99 phase should include a training component where the candidate learns new skills or techniques; the R00 phase can dovetail with the K99 project or be separate, but must be feasible and within the candidate's training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the R00 plan is unrelated to K99, clearly justify feasibility and how required resources will be obtained at the R00 institution (e.g., animal strains, subject populations, collaborators). Explain anticipated resource differences if moving to a new institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects attachment for K99/R00 with differing human subjects involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: If K99 studies do not involve human subjects/tissues but the R00 studies will, applicants should fill out the Human Subjects Attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the attachment to indicate that human subjects work will occur in the R00 phase; otherwise reviewers may expect IRB approval during K99 or consider the application incomplete. Answer to the best of your ability given anticipated future institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa certification responsibility for K99 and R00
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-U.S. citizens/permanent residents, each applicant U.S. institution (K99 or R00) must determine and document that the applicant's visa will allow them to remain in the U.S. long enough to complete the proposed K99 and/or R00 phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional certification should be explicit (example wording provided). The NICHD Grants Management Branch will verify visa extension prior to award; if visa does not permit the stay, NIH may terminate the grant. The R00 sponsoring institution must provide documentation in the transition application that the candidate will be productive for the 3 years of that award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of promotion/titles during K99
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion from postdoctoral fellow to positions such as research associate or research assistant professor may be acceptable if the PI remains dependent on the mentor's space and resources and the position does not carry privileges equivalent to regular faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles like research associate are typically OK. Positions that clearly confer independence (independent faculty/tenure-track) make the candidate ineligible. Awardees should continue searching for full-time faculty positions and notify program staff during negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent research project grants (RPGs) and K awards (including K99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may submit RPG applications (e.g., R03/R21) concurrently with a K application, but concurrent RPGs may not duplicate the provisions of the career award application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K award recipients are encouraged to obtain other funding. For K99 specifically: awardees can apply for R03/R21 but can accept salary only for effort not devoted to the K99 (maximum 25%); the allowance for shifting effort that applies to some other Ks in the last 2 years does not apply to K99. An RPG cannot be active before the K99.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension policy for K99
rubrics_metrics.description: No-cost extensions for K99 awards are only granted under unusual circumstances because K99/R00 expectations differ from conventional grants and continuity is assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request a no-cost extension submit a formal letter endorsed by the Authorized Organizational Representative addressing: documentation of efforts to obtain a faculty appointment and reasons for delay; description of progress on the career development plan; information on the appointment during the extension (title, source of support, proposed research activities). The extension does not change award terms, including the 75% effort requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for requesting R00 transition
rubrics_metrics.description: After a candidate accepts a faculty offer, the transition application must be submitted by the new institution on a PHS 398 form (the R00 is a 'type 4 revision').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the 'Revision' box on the Face Page. Submit the application and supporting documents directly to the K99 Project Officer and Grants Specialist at NICHD; they will forward the packet to the Transition Committee for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: NICHD K99/R00 Transition Committee review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Transition Committee conducts an administrative review of transition requests focusing on: (1) any modifications to the approved R00 research plan; (2) progress on the K99 training plan; and (3) aspects of the new faculty appointment and academic environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important considerations include commitments of the new department, type of faculty appointment, and start-up package. A clear formal offer or appointment letter describing the type of faculty position (e.g., tenure-track) facilitates review, particularly if staying at the same institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 transitions at the same (K99) institution
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD strongly encourages moving to an institution other than the K99 institution, but will consider same-institution R00 transitions if the candidate has made a bona fide attempt to seek other positions and the K99 institution provides the best opportunity for independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institutional commitment letter must clearly describe the type of position and details so NICHD staff can determine acceptability. The review will be stricter to ensure the position is not a temporary research appointment lacking rights and privileges of regular faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic and budgetary restrictions to consider when negotiating start-up and contracts for R00
rubrics_metrics.description: During R00 negotiation applicants must devote 75% of professional time to research (R00 project effort plus other research), and the R00 budget limit is $249,000/year (direct + indirect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear layout of duties (research vs administrative/teaching in the remaining 25%). Within the R00 budget you may request needed effort and charge the grant accordingly. R00 funds cannot be used to offset typical institutional start-up packages; institutional contributions (shared equipment, animal care, tuition, personnel) are important for transition approval. Indirect costs are not charged on equipment; if budget has a high equipment proportion, direct costs will be a higher percentage of total. NICHD can offer non-negotiation advice but will not negotiate on the applicant's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of institutional commitments and mentor contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring departments should provide formal offer or appointment letters describing the type of faculty position, start-up provisions, and assurances; mentors/collaborators should list active support in biosketches and document willingness to participate in personal statements and Item 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer letters should explicitly state tenure-track status if applicable. For tenure-track-equivalent appointments, letters must include multiple assurances describing rights and privileges. Collect and consolidate these documents in the transition application for efficient review.
